text:
sam (customer): Hey team, customer on Safari 16 sees streaming stop mid-response ~2–3s in. Server logs show full stream sent, but client gets partial text and never reconnects. Happened for ~10% of sessions after we put CloudFront in front of the API. Billing says they were charged for full request though UI shows partial output. Any ideas?

maria (support): Thanks — can you paste a HAR or a minimal repro? Is this EventSource/EventSource polyfill or using fetch streaming?

sam (customer): They use native EventSource via our frontend, no polyfill. Repro steps: open chat, trigger a long response (>6k tokens), Safari shows first chunk then stops. Network tab shows: initial GET 200 (text/event-stream), then a follow-up 304 from CloudFront during a reconnect attempt.

maria (support): Oof. 304 during EventSource reconnect sounds like caching interfering. @ajay can you weigh in on whether our edge sends Cache-Control on /stream endpoints?

ajay (eng): We set `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` across some routes to improve non-streamed payload perf; streaming endpoints should be `no-cache, no-transform`. If CloudFront revalidates and returns 304, the browser might treat the reconnect as no new body and close the connection. Need headers: `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` or at least `Cache-Control: no-cache` + `Pragma: no-cache`.

ingrid (eng-infra): Also watch `ETag`/If-None-Match flow. If edge is returning 304 for subsequent conditional GET, EventSource expects a fresh stream body. 304 has no body — that can leave client stuck waiting for events. For streaming endpoints we should not set ETag or allow revalidation.

sam (customer): Here's the raw request/response from devtools (redacted):
```
GET /v1/stream?chat_id=abc HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Accept: text/event-stream
Origin: https://app.customer.com
Connection: keep-alive

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: public, max-age=60
X-Cache: HIT from cloudfront

event: message
id: 1
data: hello

event: message
id: 2
data: ...

# later, client reconnect attempt (browser automatic):
GET /v1/stream?chat_id=abc HTTP/1.1
If-None-Match: "etag-xyz"

HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
X-Cache: REVALIDATED from cloudfront

# then client stops receiving any further chunks
```

maria (support): That matches our hypothesis. @ajay can we push quick fix to avoid ETag + make cache-control no-cache on streaming paths? Customer is seeing partial UI + gets billed for full response which is causing upset.

ajay (eng): Yes. Short-term mitigations: 1) add header on streaming endpoints: `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, proxy-revalidate` and remove `ETag`. 2) Set `Vary: Accept` or a cache key that includes `Accept` to prevent caching by general GET. 3) Make CloudFront behavior for `/v1/stream*` forward all headers and not cache. I'll open a deploy.

ingrid (eng-infra): Also we should emit `Retry: 2000` SSE comment or use `id:` values and rely on Last-Event-ID. Note: Last-Event-ID is only respected if the server returns a full body on reconnect — which 304 prevents. For Safari specifically, there are known quirks where a 204/304 on reconnect will cause EventSource to never fire `onopen` again.

sam (customer): Any client-side workarounds we can tell them to do while we fix the edge?

ajay (eng): Yes — two options: 1) append a cache-busting query param to the SSE URL on each connect (e.g., `?t=Date.now()`) so CDN treats it as unique. Ugly but fast. 2) Use an EventSource polyfill that uses XHR streaming or fetch streaming fallback for Safari — that avoids the native reconnect behavior quirks. Example polyfill: `eventsource-polyfill` or `@microsoft/fetch-event-source`.

maria (support): Can you give a short repro command we can share with the customer (curl) so they can confirm server side is correct?

ajay (eng): Sure — curl can show chunked SSE flow:
```bash
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Origin: https://app.customer.com" \
  "https://api.example.com/v1/stream?chat_id=abc"
```
The `-N` (no-buffer) preserves chunked output. You should see `event:` lines streaming. If you instead see `HTTP/1.1 304` then edge is revalidating.

sam (customer): We ran that and saw identical: initial streaming then if connection restarts the edge answers 304. We'll ask them to add the cache-buster param for now.

ingrid (eng-infra): Deploy plan: I'll push CloudFront behavior update to bypass cache for `/v1/stream*` and drop ETag from origin responses for that path. Quick rollback ready. ETA ~ 45m.

agey (deploy-bot): deploy started for edge-config "no-cache-streams" (change set 42) — watching health.

ajay (eng): Follow-up checklist for platform: 1) Ensure `Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8` present. 2) No `ETag` or `Last-Modified` for streams. 3) `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate`. 4) Consider adding small keepalive comments from origin like `: keepalive\n\n` every 15s to prevent intermediate proxies from closing idle connections.

maria (support): Thanks — I'll update the customer with the workaround (cache-buster or polyfill) and tell them we rolled an edge fix. Please post here when CloudFront change is healthy. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded (change set 42) — distribution updated in 32s.

ajay (eng): Confirmed with curl after change: reconnection returns 200 and stream resumes (no 304). Safari repro fixed on our QA device.

sam (customer): Customer confirmed fixed on their side too. They were able to reproduce before and now no partial outputs. They patched frontend with cache-buster as a temporary measure. Thanks everyone.

maria (support): Closing this thread once we send a follow-up note about billing/prorate options for the affected sessions. Also will add docs note: "Streaming endpoints must not be cached by CDN" and include the curl repro + header examples.

ajay (eng): I'll also add a test in our e2e harness that sends SSE from behind CloudFront to catch regressions.

sam (customer): Appreciate the fast turn. :raised_hands:
